chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the man who fights for his wealth, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Whoever is killed protecting his wealth, he is in the rank of a martyr.' We said to him (peace be upon him): 'So is fighting better?' He said: 'If you do not fight, there is no problem. As for me, if it were me, I would leave him and not fight.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on fighting to protect one's wealth and does it grant martyrdom?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the distinction between the general prophetic promise of martyrdom for defending one's property and the specific juristic preference (istihbab) of Imam al-Sadiq to prioritize peace over conflict. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on voluntary acts of virtue rather than strict obligation, illustrating the Imam's personal asceticism by choosing to forgo the fight even when he had the capacity to do so.
